findings.description: The reports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default, unlike the audit bucket in the same file.

No ACL is specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so nothing in the configuration prevents a public ACL or bucket policy being applied to a bucket that holds vendor data.
No logging block is configured, so object access to this data bucket is not recorded, removing the audit trail needed to detect unauthorised access.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably, destroying evidence of tampering.
The ledger export bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored without enforced default encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket; the private ACL alone does not prevent a later bucket policy or ACL change from exposing ledger data publicly.
No server access logging is configured for a bucket containing financial ledger exports, so unauthorised reads would go unrecorded.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or permanently deleted with no recovery path.
The model artifacts bucket has no default server-side encryption configuration, so stored artifacts are not protected by an enforced SSE-KMS default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies for this bucket, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults.
The runbooks bucket, which typically holds operational procedures and credential-adjacent internal detail, defines no default server-side encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against subsequent public ACL or policy grants.
No logging block is configured for the runbooks bucket, so access to sensitive operational documentation is not audited.
The audit log destination bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; a misapplied ACL or policy could expose accumulated access logs, revealing access patterns to an attacker.
The audit trail bucket sets force_destroy = true and configures no object lock or MFA delete, so the central log store can be emptied and destroyed in a single apply, defeating its integrity purpose.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/contact data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which itself lacks default encryption, so the object is stored unencrypted.

No bucket policy on any bucket in this file denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects may be read or written over cleartext HTTP. Reported once against the primary data bucket; the same gap applies to ledger_exports, model_artifacts, ops_runbooks and audit_trail.
